title: Little Ḥiṣṣa and baby Ḥammūd
goal: At Sēf's family home, with Sēf, meet his little niece again and find out the pet names the family uses
tip: Gulf Arabic makes words small and dear: ṣghīr 'small' → ṣghayyir 'tiny', bint 'girl' → bnayya 'little girl'. Names do it too: Muḥammad → Ḥammūd, Sālim → Sallūm, Maryam → Maryūm. Use a pet name for someone only after their family uses it in front of you, and never for a woman outside your family.
grammar: diminutives: ṣghīr → ṣghayyir, bint → bnayya; pet names (Ḥammūd, Sallūm)
dialogue: A
تعال، شوف منو هني! تذكر حصة، بنت أخوي؟
taʿāl, shūf minu hni! tidhkir Ḥiṣṣa, bint akhūy?
Come in, look who's here! Do you remember Ḥiṣṣa, my brother's daughter?
B
ما شاء الله! كبرت وايد
mā shāʼ allāh! kibrat wāyid
Mā shāʼ allāh! She's grown so much.
A
هيه، هالبنية صارت تروح المدرسة، بس تستحي شوي من الناس
hē, hal-bnayya ṣārat trūḥ il-madrasa, bas tistiḥi shwayy min in-nās
Yes, this little girl goes to school now, but she's a bit shy with people.
B
عادي. حصة، تذكريني؟ أنا سالم
ʿādi. Ḥiṣṣa, tidhkrīni? ana Sālim
That's fine. Ḥiṣṣa, do you remember me? I'm Sālim.
A
قولي له: هلا عمي سلوم! كلنا نسميه سلوم، أمي تقول سالم وايد رسمي
gūlī-lah: hala ʿammi Sallūm! killna nsammīh Sallūm, ummi tgūl Sālim wāyid rasmi
Say to him: 'Hi, Uncle Sallūm!' We all call him Sallūm; my mum says Sālim is too formal.
B
سلوم؟! زين. وهذا البيبي الصغيّر محمد؟
Sallūm?! zēn. w hādha l-bēbi ṣ-ṣghayyir Muḥammad?
Sallūm?! OK. And this tiny little baby is Muḥammad?
A
هيه، ولد أختي. بس الكل يقول له حمود، حتى أمه وأبوه
hē, wild ukhti. bas il-kill ygūl-lah Ḥammūd, ḥatta ummah w ubūh
Yes, my sister's boy. But everyone calls him Ḥammūd, even his mum and dad.
B
ما شاء الله عليه! الله يخليه لكم
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēh! allāh ykhallīh lakum
Mā shāʼ allāh! God bless him for you all.
A
الله يخليك. تفضل اقعد
allāh ykhallīk. tfaẓẓal igʿid
Thank you. Please, sit down.
items: the small, loving form of bint; an older relative calls a girl yā bnayyti (يا بنيتي) (recognise)
she's shy; you're shy (to a man)
to a woman: tistiḥīn (تستحين); I'm shy: astiḥi (أستحي)
she's grown so much, she's got so big
he's grown so much: kibar wāyid (كبر وايد)
my sister's daughter: bint ukhti (بنت أختي)
everyone calls her: il-kill ygūl-lha (الكل يقول لها) (recognise)
ṣghayyir is the loving small form of ṣghīr; UAE also: il-yāhil (الياهل) 'the child'
even her mum and dad: ḥatta umm-ha w ubūha (حتى أمها وأبوها)
task: This week: search YouTube for «مسلسل إماراتي» (Emirati series) and watch one family scene. Listen for pet names (like Ḥammūd or Maryūm) and for yā ʿammi, yā khālti, yā wildi. Write down three, and who says each one to whom. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب; if you hear سوف, ليس or هل all the time, it's fuṣḥā: pick another clip.

title: Why 'Bū Rāshid'?
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis in Sharjah, with Sēf there, ask why everyone calls him Bū Rāshid, and what you'd be called
tip: A man is often called bū (father of) + his eldest son's name, a woman umm + the son's name: Bū Rāshid, Umm Sēf. Call him with yā: yā Bū Rāshid. 'So-and-so' is fulān: yā bū fulān 'So-and-so's dad'.
grammar: abu / umm: bū + son's name (yā Bū Rāshid); fulān 'so-and-so'
dialogue: B
مساء الخير يا بو راشد
masāʼ il-khēr yā Bū Rāshid
Good evening, Bū Rāshid.
A
مساء النور! حياك الله يا ولدي
masāʼ in-nūr! ḥayyāk allāh yā wildi
Good evening! Welcome, son.
B
الله يحييك. شحالك يا عمي؟
allāh yḥayyīk. shḥālak yā ʿammi?
Thank you. How are you, uncle?
A
بخير الله يسلمك. ما شاء الله، صرت تقول بو راشد مثلنا!
b-khēr, allāh ysallmak. mā shāʼ allāh, ṣirt tgūl Bū Rāshid mithilna!
Fine, thank you. Mā shāʼ allāh, you've started saying Bū Rāshid like us!
B
هيه! بس ليش الكل يقول لك بو راشد، مب باسمك؟
hē! bas lēsh il-kill ygūl-lak Bū Rāshid, mub b-ismak?
Yes! But why does everyone call you Bū Rāshid, not by your name?
A
عندنا الريّال ينادونه على اسم ولده الكبير، وراشد أكبر عيالي
ʿindana r-rayyāl ynādūnah ʿala ism wildah il-kbīr, w Rāshid akbar ʿyāli
Here we call a man after his eldest son, and Rāshid is my eldest.
B
وأنا؟ ما عندي عيال!
w ana? ma ʿindi ʿyāl!
And me? I haven't got any children!
A
في ناس ما عندهم عيال وعندهم اسم. خالد مثلا يقولون له بو وليد
fī nās ma ʿindahum ʿyāl w ʿindahum ism. Khālid mathalan ygūlūn-lah Bū Walīd
Some people have no children and still get one. Any Khālid, for example, gets called Bū Walīd.
B
زين، ويوم يصير عندي ولد؟
zēn, w yōm yṣīr ʿindi wild?
OK, and when I have a son?
A
لا تستعيل! يوم تعرس ويصير عندك ولد، بنقول لك يا بو فلان
la tistaʿyil! yōm tʿarris w yṣīr ʿindak wild, bingūl-lak yā bū fulān
Don't rush! When you get married and have a son, we'll call you 'Bū So-and-so'.
items: Bū Rāshid! (respectful: a man called by his son's name)
any man: yā bū + his eldest son's name; a woman: yā umm + the son's name (يا أم …)
after his son, named after his son
after her son: ʿala ism wild-ha (على اسم ولدها) (recognise)
my eldest (child), the eldest of my children
when you get married (to a man)
to a woman: yōm tʿarrsīn (يوم تعرسين)
he gets called Bū Walīd (a name Khālids often get)
culture: A man is often known as Bū (father of) + the name of his first son, and a woman as Umm + that son's name. Saying it is warm and respectful, and it is often how people address him in the majlis. A man with no son can still have one: a Khālid, for example, is often called Bū Walīd.

title: Yā ʿammi, yā ukhti, yā shēkh
goal: In the car with Sēf, after you call an old man yā ḥabībi, find out how to address people of every age and rank
tip: Pick the word by age and rank: an older man yā ʿammi or yā l-wālid, a man your age yā akhūy, a woman you don't know yā ukhti, a sheikh ṭāl ʿumrak or yā shēkh. yā rayyāl and yā ḥabībi are for friends.
grammar: forms of address: yā l-wālid, yā akhūy, yā ukhti, yā shēkh. Recycle: yā ʿammi, ṭāl ʿumrak
dialogue: A
شو قلت للشيبة في المحطة؟ يا حبيبي؟!
shu gilt lish-shēba fi l-maḥaṭṭa? yā ḥabībi?!
What did you say to the old man at the petrol station? 'Yā ḥabībi'?!
B
هيه... غلط؟
hē… ghalaṭ?
Yes… is that wrong?
A
مب غلط وايد، بس للشيبة قول يا عمي، أو يا الوالد
mub ghalaṭ wāyid, bas lish-shēba gūl yā ʿammi, aw yā l-wālid
Not very, but to an old man say yā ʿammi, or yā l-wālid.
B
زين. والريّال اللي في الكرك؟ يا أخوي؟
zēn. w ir-rayyāl illi fi l-karak? yā akhūy?
OK. And the man at the karak stand? Yā akhūy?
A
هيه، يا أخوي أو يا الحبيب. بس يا ريّال خلها لي ولفهد!
hē, yā akhūy aw yā l-ḥabīb. bas yā rayyāl khallha li w li-Fahad!
Yes, yā akhūy or yā l-ḥabīb. But save yā rayyāl for me and Fahad!
B
والبنت اللي في الصيدلية؟
w il-bint illi fi ṣ-ṣēdaliyya?
And the girl at the pharmacy?
A
قول لها يا أختي، وكلمها على قد الشغل
gūl-lha yā ukhti, w kallimha ʿala gadd ish-shughul
Say yā ukhti to her, and keep it to the business.
B
وإذا شفت شيخ؟
w idha shift shēkh?
And if I meet a sheikh?
A
قول له طال عمرك، أو يا شيخ. هذا أحسن شي مع الشيوخ
gūl-lah ṭāl ʿumrak, aw yā shēkh. hādha aḥsan shay maʿa sh-shyūkh
Say ṭāl ʿumrak, or yā shēkh. That's best with sheikhs.
B
يعني لكل واحد كلمة!
yaʿni l-kill wāḥid kilma!
So everyone gets their own word!
items: sir (respectful, to an older man; lit. father)
to an older woman: yā l-wālda (يا الوالدة)
excuse me, brother (polite, to a man your age; lit. my brother)
to a woman: yā ukhti (يا أختي)
excuse me (polite, to a woman you don't know; lit. my sister)
to a man: yā akhūy (يا أخوي)
to a sheikha: yā shēkha (يا شيخة)
my friend, mate (friendly, to a man in a shop or café)
if I see, if I meet; if you see (to a man)
to a woman: idha shifti (إذا شفتي)
only as far as the business needs, keep it to the job
culture: How you address someone shows respect. Elders and strangers get yā ʿammi or ṭāl ʿumrak; yā rayyāl is for friends, and saying it to an elder or in a meeting comes across as very rude. With young people you know, English words and bro are fine; with elders, keep your Arabic unmixed.

title: Yā salām! Shkubur-ha!
goal: Sēf turns up in his brother's new car: show how impressed you are, and how lucky his brother is
tip: To say 'how big!' or 'how lovely!', put sh- on a noun with an ending: shkubur-ha! 'how big it (f.) is!', shḥalātah! 'how lovely he/it is!'. Add yā salām! 'wow!' and yā ḥaẓẓah! 'lucky him!'.
grammar: exclamatives: yā salām!, sh- + noun + ending (shkubur-ha!, shḥalāt-ha!), yā ḥaẓẓah!
dialogue: A
شوف! أخوي خلاني أسوق سيارته اليديدة اليوم
shūf! akhūy khallāni asūg sayyārtah il-yidīda l-yōm
Look! My brother's let me drive his new car today.
B
يا سلام! شكبرها!
yā salām! shkubur-ha!
Wow! How big it is!
A
وايد حلوة، صح؟ وداخلها أحلى
wāyid ḥilwa, ṣaḥḥ? w dākhil-ha aḥla
Really nice, isn't it? And it's even nicer inside.
B
مبروك عليه! شحلاتها! يا حظ أخوك
mabrūk ʿalēh! shḥalāt-ha! yā ḥaẓẓ akhūk
Congratulations to him! How lovely it is! Your brother's so lucky.
A
الله يبارك فيك! بس لا تسألني كم دفع فيها، ولا تسأله هو بعد!
allāh ybārik fīk! bas la tisʼalni cham dafaʿ fīha, wala tisʼalah huwa baʿad!
Thanks! But don't ask me how much he paid for it, and don't ask him either!
B
لا تقول! أكيد وايد
la tgūl! akīd wāyid
Don't tell me! It must be a lot.
A
شكثر هو مستانس عليها! كل يوم يغسلها، حليله!
shkuthur huwa mistānis ʿalēha! kill yōm yighsilha, ḥalīlah!
He's so happy with it! He washes it every day, bless him!
B
يا حظه! سيارتي صغيرة وقديمة
yā ḥaẓẓah! sayyārti ṣghīra w gadīma
Lucky him! My car's small and old.
A
عادي! المهم إنها توصلك
ʿādi! il-muhimm innha twaṣṣlak
So what! What matters is it gets you where you're going.
B
صدقت والله!
ṣidagt wallāh!
Too true!
items: how lovely it (f.) is! how sweet she is!
your brother's so lucky (to a man)
to a woman: yā ḥaẓẓ akhūch (يا حظ أخوج)
lucky her: yā ḥaẓẓ-ha! (يا حظها); lucky you: yā ḥaẓẓak! (to a man), yā ḥaẓẓich! (to a woman)
before a sentence: shkuthur huwa mistānis! 'he's so happy!'; to ask a price, say cham (كم) (recognise)
don't tell me! no way! (to a man)
to a woman: la tgūlīn! (لا تقولين)
bless him! (said fondly, or with pity) (UAE)

title: Lunch with Umm Sēf
goal: At Sēf's home, with Sēf there, greet his mother by her kunya, pass on your mum's regards and thank her for lunch
tip: To a friend's mother, yā khālti is warm and yā umm Sēf is warm and respectful. Pass on regards with ummi tsallim ʿalēch 'my mum says hello (to you, f.)'; the answer is allāh ysallimha.
grammar: address in practice: yā umm Sēf, yā khālti; recycle: yā salām, shḥalāt-, ḥalīl-
dialogue: A
هلا والله! حياك الله يا ولدي، تفضل خذ راحتك
hala wallāh! ḥayyāk allāh yā wildi, tfaẓẓal khidh rāḥtak
Hello! Welcome, son, come in and make yourself at home.
B
الله يحييج يا أم سيف. شحالج؟
allāh yḥayyīch yā Umm Sēf. shḥālich?
Thank you, Umm Sēf. How are you?
A
بخير الله يسلمك. وشحال أمك؟ إن شاء الله بخير
b-khēr, allāh ysallmak. w shḥāl ummak? in shāʼ allāh b-khēr
Fine, thank you. And how's your mother? Well, I hope.
B
بخير الحمد لله. أمي تسلّم عليج وايد
b-khēr il-ḥamdu lillāh. ummi tsallim ʿalēch wāyid
She's well, thank God. My mum sends you her warm regards.
A
الله يسلمها! يا حليلها. متى بتزورنا؟
allāh ysallimha! yā ḥalīlha. mita bitzūrna?
God keep her! Bless her. When's she going to visit us?
B
إن شاء الله الصيف الياي، يمكن
in shāʼ allāh iṣ-ṣēf il-yāy, yimkin
Next summer, God willing, maybe.
A
زين! يلا، الغدا على السفرة. سيف قال إنك تحب المكبوس
zēn! yalla, il-ghada ʿala s-sufra. Sēf gāl innak tḥibb il-machbūs
Good! Come on, lunch is on the table. Sēf said you like machbūs.
B
يا سلام على الريحة! تفتح النفس. تسلمين يا خالتي
yā salām ʿala r-rīḥa! tiftaḥ in-nafs. tislamīn yā khālti
What a lovely smell! It makes me hungry. Thank you, auntie.
A
الله يسلمك. بالعافية يا ولدي
allāh ysallmak. bil-ʿāfya yā wildi
You're welcome. Enjoy your food, son.
B
الله يعافيج
allāh yʿāfīch
Thank you.
items: Umm Sēf! (respectful, to a woman by her son's name)
any woman: yā umm + her son's name (يا أم …)
to a woman: shḥāl ummich? (شحال أمج؟)
machbūs (spiced rice with meat, chicken or fish)
when will she visit us? when will you visit us? (to a man)
to a woman: mita bitzūrīnna? (متى بتزورينا؟) (recognise)
on the table, served (of a meal)
make yourself at home, make yourself comfortable (to a man)
to a woman: khidhi rāḥtich (خذي راحتج) (recognise)
it makes you hungry, it whets your appetite
culture: Machbūs, rice cooked with spices and meat, chicken or fish, is one of the classic Emirati dishes. Admire the food (yā salām ʿala r-rīḥa!) and thank the cook: tislamīn to a woman, tislam to a man, or tislam īdich 'bless your hands' to the woman who cooked it.

title: He must be in a meeting
goal: At the office, help Maryam guess why the manager hasn't answered her: lāzim ykūn, yimkin kān, la ykūn…?
tip: Guess with ykūn and kān: lāzim ykūn fi ijtimāʿ 'he must be in a meeting', yimkin kān mashghūl 'maybe he was busy'. A worried guess: la ykūn zaʿlān? 'he isn't cross, is he?'. Future: biykūn mitfahhim 'he'll be understanding'.
grammar: kān / ykūn strings: lāzim ykūn, yimkin kān, la ykūn…?, biykūn + participle
dialogue: A
سالم، بو سعيد ما رد على إيميلي من الصبح
Sālim, Bū Saʿīd ma radd ʿala īmēli min iṣ-ṣubḥ
Sālim, Bū Saʿīd hasn't answered my email since this morning.
B
لازم يكون في اجتماع
lāzim ykūn fi ijtimāʿ
He must be in a meeting.
A
ما أظن، اليوم ما عنده اجتماعات
ma aẓunn, il-yōm ma ʿindah ijtimāʿāt
I don't think so, he hasn't got any meetings today.
B
يمكن كان مشغول وايد، يمكن نسى
yimkin kān mashghūl wāyid, yimkin nisa
Maybe he was really busy, maybe he forgot.
A
لا يكون زعلان مني؟ أمس قلت له إن التقرير بيتأخر
la ykūn zaʿlān minni? ams gilt-lah inn it-taqrīr biyitʼakhkhar
He isn't cross with me, is he? Yesterday I told him the report would be late.
B
لا أبد! أكيد بيكون متفهم
la abad! akīd biykūn mitfahhim
Not at all! I'm sure he'll understand.
A
إن شاء الله. خلني أتصل في سكرتيرته وأسألها
in shāʼ allāh. khallni attaṣil fi sikritērtah w asʼalha
I hope so. Let me ring his secretary and ask her.
B
زين. يمكن يكون طالع
zēn. yimkin ykūn ṭāliʿ
OK. Maybe he's out.
A
صدقت والله! طلع عنده موعد عند الدكتور من الصبح!
ṣidagt wallāh! ṭilaʿ ʿindah mawʿid ʿind id-daktōr min iṣ-ṣubḥ!
You were right! It turns out he had a doctor's appointment this morning!
B
يعني مب زعلان منج أبد!
yaʿni mub zaʿlān minnich abad!
So he's not cross with you at all!
items: he must be, it must be (a guess)
she must be: lāzim tkūn (لازم تكون)
maybe he was, maybe it was
maybe she was: yimkin kānat (يمكن كانت)
maybe he is, he might be
she might be: yimkin tkūn (يمكن تكون)
he isn't cross, is he? (a worried guess)
of a woman: la tkūn zaʿlāna? (لا تكون زعلانة؟); not the same as la tkūn zaʿlān 'don't be cross' (to a man)
she'll be understanding: bitkūn mitfahhma (بتكون متفهمة)
maybe she forgot: yimkin nisat (يمكن نست); maybe I forgot: yimkin nisēt (يمكن نسيت)
it turns out he has an appointment
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor»), look at three photos of people together. For each, guess aloud who they are and what's going on, with lāzim ykūn, yimkin kān and aẓunn. Ask your partner which guesses sounded natural, and note one thing they'd say differently.

title: He drives as if he's in a race
goal: At a karak stand with Sēf, laugh at a show-off driver and at each other: chinnah, chinnak, awinna
tip: chinn- 'as if, like' takes an ending: chinnah fi sibāg 'as if he's in a race', chinnak ma rgadt 'you look as if you didn't sleep', chinni 'as if I'. awinna! mocks a claim: 'as if! yeah, right!' (UAE).
grammar: "as if": chinnah / chinnak / chinni + clause; awinna (UAE, mocking)
dialogue: A
شوف هذا! يسوق كنه في سباق، كن الشارع حقه
shūf hādha! ysūg chinnah fi sibāg, chinn ish-shāriʿ ḥaggah
Look at him! He drives as if he's in a race, as if the street's his.
B
صج! أونه هو أحسن واحد يسوق!
ṣij! awinna huwa aḥsan wāḥid ysūg!
True! As if he's the best driver around!
A
ها! بس انت أمس كنت تسوق نفس الشي!
hā! bas inta ams kint tsūg nafs ish-shay!
Ha! But you were driving the same way yesterday!
B
أنا؟! لا أبد. أنا أسوق شوي شوي
ana?! la abad. ana asūg shwayy shwayy
Me?! Not at all. I drive slowly.
A
أونه! شوي شوي؟ كنك طيارة!
awinna! shwayy shwayy? chinnak ṭayyāra!
Yeah, right! Slowly? You're like a plane!
B
زين زين. خلنا نشرب الكرك
zēn zēn. khallna nishrab il-karak
OK, OK. Let's drink our karak.
A
بس انت شفيك اليوم؟ كنك ما رقدت
bas inta shfīk il-yōm? chinnak ma rgadt
But what's up with you today? You look as if you didn't sleep.
B
صج، ما نمت عدل. عندي امتحان باكر
ṣij, ma nimt ʿadil. ʿindi imtiḥān bāchir
True, I didn't sleep properly. I've got an exam tomorrow.
A
لا تحاتي، بتنجح إن شاء الله
la tḥāti, bitinjaḥ in shāʼ allāh
Don't worry, you'll pass, God willing.
B
إن شاء الله. بس أحس كني ما ذاكرت شي!
in shāʼ allāh. bas aḥiss chinni ma dhākart shay!
I hope so. But I feel as if I haven't revised anything!
items: as if she: chinnha (كنها); you'll see written جنه; some say kinnah
you look as if, you're like (to a man)
as if I, (I feel) like I
as if! yeah, right! (mocking what someone claims) (UAE)
as if he owns the street, as if the street's his
you didn't sleep (to a man); I didn't sleep (UAE)
to a woman: ma rgadti (ما رقدتي); everywhere: ma nimt (ما نمت)
I feel as if I, it feels like I

title: I reckon I passed
goal: After the exam, tell Sēf what you'd thought, what you expect, and what you don't believe: atwaggaʿ, ʿala bāli, ma aʿtagid
tip: Gulf has a word for each kind of thinking: atwaggaʿ inn 'I expect', aẓunn 'I think', aḥiss 'I feel', ma aʿtagid 'I don't believe so', and ʿala bāli or ẓannēt 'I thought (but I was wrong)': ʿala bāli biykūn sahil.
grammar: "I think" expressions: atwaggaʿ inn, ʿala bāli / ẓannēt (thought wrongly), ma aʿtagid. Recycle: aẓunn, aḥiss, titwaggaʿ
dialogue: A
ها، كيف كان الامتحان؟
hā, chēf kān il-imtiḥān?
So, how was the exam?
B
على بالي بيكون سهل، بس طلع صعب!
ʿala bāli biykūn sahil, bas ṭilaʿ ṣaʿb!
I thought it would be easy, but it turned out hard!
A
تتوقع إنك نجحت؟
titwaggaʿ innak nijaḥt?
Do you reckon you passed?
B
أتوقع إني نجحت، بس الدرجة ما أظن بتكون عالية
atwaggaʿ inni nijaḥt, bas id-daraja ma aẓunn bitkūn ʿālya
I reckon I passed, but I don't think the mark will be high.
A
عادي! وأنا ظنيت انت دوم الأول
ʿādi! w ana ẓannēt inta dōm il-awwal
That's OK! And I thought you always came top.
B
لا يا ريّال! أحس الكل أشطر مني هالسنة
la yā rayyāl! aḥiss il-kill ashṭar minni has-sana
No, man! I feel everyone's cleverer than me this year.
A
ما أعتقد. وشو قال الدكتور؟ متى النتايج؟
ma aʿtagid. w shu gāl id-daktōr? mita n-natāyij?
I don't believe that. And what did the professor say? When are the results?
B
قال إن النتايج بتطلع الأسبوع الياي
gāl inn in-natāyij bitiṭlaʿ il-usbūʿ il-yāy
He said the results will come out next week.
A
خلاص، لا تفكر فيه. أتوقع إنك بتستانس
khalāṣ, la tfakkir fīh. atwaggaʿ innak bitistānis
Right, don't think about it. I reckon you'll be pleased.
B
إن شاء الله، والباقي على الله
in shāʼ allāh, w il-bāgi ʿala llāh
God willing, and the rest is up to God.
items: don't think about it, put it out of your mind (to a man)
to a woman: la tfakkrīn fīh (لا تفكرين فيه)
I don't believe so, I don't think so
a little more formal than ma aẓunn (ما أظن)
it (f.) turned out hard: ṭilʿat ṣaʿba (طلعت صعبة)
cleverer than me, better than me (at studies)
and the rest is up to God

title: They don't talk to each other
goal: With Sēf, find out why two classmates have fallen out, and plan to get them to make up: baʿaẓ, kill wāḥid … ith-thāni
tip: 'Each other' is baʿaẓ after a plural verb: ma ykallmūn baʿaẓ 'they don't talk to each other', biyshūfūn baʿaẓ 'they'll see each other'. Or say it in two halves: kill wāḥid ylūm ith-thāni 'each one blames the other'.
grammar: reciprocals: verb + baʿaẓ (ma ykallmūn baʿaẓ), kill wāḥid … ith-thāni, mitzāʿlīn
dialogue: A
تدري إن أحمد وحمد متزاعلين؟
tadri inn Aḥmad w Ḥamad mitzāʿlīn?
Did you know Aḥmad and Ḥamad have fallen out?
B
لا! بس هم دوم ويا بعض!
la! bas hum dōm wiyya baʿaẓ!
No! But they're always together!
A
كانوا. بس من أسبوع ما يكلمون بعض
kānaw. bas min usbūʿ ma ykallmūn baʿaẓ
They were. But they haven't spoken to each other for a week.
B
ليش؟ شو صار بينهم؟
lēsh? shu ṣār bēnhum?
Why? What happened between them?
A
المشروع! كل واحد يلوم الثاني، ويقول إنه ما سوى شي
il-mashrūʿ! kill wāḥid ylūm ith-thāni, w ygūl innah ma sawwa shay
The project! Each one blames the other and says he did nothing.
B
خسارة! هم يعرفون بعض من المدرسة
khasāra! hum yaʿarfūn baʿaẓ min il-madrasa
What a shame! They've known each other since school.
A
صح، ويحبون بعض وايد. لازم نسوي شي
ṣaḥḥ, w yḥibbūn baʿaẓ wāyid. lāzim nsawwi shay
Right, and they really like each other. We have to do something.
B
نعزمهم على عشا، وكل واحد يعتذر للثاني
nʿazmhum ʿala ʿasha, w kill wāḥid yiʿtadhir lith-thāni
Let's invite them to dinner, and each one apologises to the other.
A
فكرة حلوة! بس لا نقول لهم إنهم بيشوفون بعض
fikra ḥilwa! bas la ngūl-lhum innhum biyshūfūn baʿaẓ
Good idea! But let's not tell them they'll be seeing each other.
B
أكيد! خلها مفاجأة
akīd! khallha mufājaʼa
Of course! Keep it a surprise.
items: fallen out, not speaking (two people or more)
two women: mitzāʿlāt (متزاعلات); one person: zaʿlān (upset)
they don't talk to each other
we don't talk: ma nkallim baʿaẓ (ما نكلم بعض)
they like each other, they love each other
let's invite them, we'll invite them
we'll see each other: binshūf baʿaẓ (بنشوف بعض)

title: Personally, I didn't like it
goal: At the office, give Maryam your honest view of the new system, with examples: shakhṣiyyan, mathalan, khuṣūṣan
tip: Words ending in -an work like English -ly: shakhṣiyyan 'personally', mathalan 'for example', khuṣūṣan 'especially', tamāman 'completely', fiʿlan 'really'. You already know tagrīban, ṭabʿan and aṣlan. Write them with ا, no extra mark.
grammar: -an adverbs: shakhṣiyyan, mathalan, khuṣūṣan, tamāman, fiʿlan, dāyman. Recycle: tagrīban, ṭabʿan, aṣlan
dialogue: A
سالم، بو سعيد يبي رأيك في البرنامج اليديد
Sālim, Bū Saʿīd yabi raʼyak fi l-barnāmij il-yidīd
Sālim, Bū Saʿīd wants your opinion on the new system.
B
بصراحة؟ شخصيا ما حبيته وايد
b-ṣarāḥa? shakhṣiyyan ma ḥabbētah wāyid
Honestly? Personally, I didn't like it much.
A
ليش؟ أنا شفته سهل تقريبا
lēsh? ana shiftah sahil tagrīban
Why? I found it more or less easy.
B
سهل، بس بطيء. مثلا التقارير تاخذ وايد وقت
sahil, bas baṭīʼ. mathalan it-taqārīr tākhidh wāyid wagt
Easy, but slow. For example, the reports take ages.
A
صح، خصوصا الصبح لما الكل يشتغل عليه
ṣaḥḥ, khuṣūṣan iṣ-ṣubḥ lamma l-kill yishtaghil ʿalēh
True, especially in the morning when everyone's working on it.
B
بالضبط! وأمس خرب تماما ساعة كاملة
biẓ-ẓabṭ! w ams khirab tamāman sāʿa kāmla
Exactly! And yesterday it broke down completely for a whole hour.
A
فعلا؟ ما دريت! حاليا الشركة تدور على برنامج ثاني
fiʿlan? ma dirēt! ḥāliyyan ish-sharika tdawwir ʿala barnāmij thāni
Really? I didn't know! At the moment the company's looking for another system.
B
زين. بس لا تقولين له إني قلت جي!
zēn. bas la tgūlīn-lah inni gilt chī!
Good. But don't tell him I said so!
A
لا تحاتي! هو يبي رأي الكل، وأخيرا أحد يقول رأيه بصراحة
la tḥāti! huwa yabi raʼy il-kill, w akhīran aḥad ygūl raʼyah b-ṣarāḥa
Don't worry! He wants everyone's opinion, and at last someone's giving his honestly.
B
أنا دايما أقول اللي في قلبي
ana dāyman agūl illi fi galbi
I always say what's on my mind.
items: what's on my mind, what I really think (lit. what's in my heart)
